description: Puts screens on the design canvas of one of the user's Better Design projects, as editable frames. The owner sees them when they open the canvas, and can then move, resize and retype every layer by hand. Use it for four jobs. A user journey: one step for each screen of the flow, in order, with the happy path first and its loading, empty and error states under it in the same step; take the steps from the feature map when the repository has one, and give each frame the `next` frames it leads to, so the canvas draws the flow's arrows. Design options: one step for each option, so they sit side by side. Component usage: one step for each screen that uses the component. States: one step, with every state of one screen. Send the real screen: render it, then pass its HTML with the CSS it needs in a <style> block. The canvas draws boxes, text, borders, radii and inline SVG. It does not draw pictures, gradients or shadows yet. One call takes up to 24 frames. Call again for a longer flow.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

height.description: Only for a screen that fills its window, such as one with a bar fixed to the bottom: the window height in pixels. Left out, the frame is as tall as its content.

html.description: The screen as HTML that carries its own CSS in a <style> block or inline styles. No script runs and nothing loads from the network.

name.description: The frame's name on the canvas, such as "Cart, loading".

next.description: The names of the frames in this call that this one leads to, such as ["Payment"]. The canvas draws an arrow to each one, as a prototype does.

step.description: The column this frame sits in. Frames with the same step stack top to bottom, and steps run left to right in the order they first appear.

width.description: The width to render at, in pixels. Defaults to 1440. Use 390 for a phone screen.

projectId.description: The id of the project whose canvas to draw on, from create-design-system or the address of the project page.

title.description: What this drawing shows, such as "Checkout flow".

name: draw-on-canvas
title: Draw Screens on the Canvas
